summary: The note traces esports history from 1970s-80s arcade games through the internet, streaming, corporate sponsorship, and academic and governmental recognition to today's global tournaments. It covers technology, community, niche markets, investment and inclusivity as drivers of growth. It concludes that esports will keep growing and redefining sport, competition and community.
one_line: A historical overview of esports milestones from arcades to global tournaments, with predictions of continued growth, diversification, investment and inclusivity.
key_facts: The 1970s and 1980s saw the birth of competitive video gaming with titles like 'Space Invaders' and 'Pac-Man'.
The 1990 Nintendo World Championships traveled across the United States, crowning the best players in video game challenges.
'Quake' was released on September 30, 1997, and its online multiplayer mode laid the foundation for professional gaming leagues.
Major League Gaming was established in 2002, giving esports structure and standards akin to traditional sports.
YouTube began in 2005 and Twitch emerged in 2011, helping live gameplay sharing and audiences grow.
On July 17, 2014, the 'League of Legends' Championship Series broadcast achieved mainstream coverage.
On September 4, 2015, 'ESPN' featured 'The International Dota 2 Championships', and brands like Coca-Cola and Red Bull invested in esports marketing and sponsorship.
The National Association of Collegiate Esports was formed in 2017, giving governance on par with NCAA sports.
On September 8, 2018, South Korea created policies to support the esports industry.
The 2021 'Fortnite' World Cup had a $30 million prize pool.
Esports was a demonstration event at the Asian Games in 2018 and a medal event in 2022.
The PS5 was released in 2020 and was quickly embraced by the competitive gaming community.
The 'Mobile Legends' Championship Series was launched on September 2, 2023, signaling mobile gaming's growing clout.
Emily "Emz" Peters, interviewed September 15, 2023, said digital competition has opened opportunities for diverse players that were not possible before.
